_help.about: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, LOCKED by Mike: the underground fire ventilation rule, design §EV; TombKit places them, TombBuild carves them, Vents lights them) Every permanent fire the dungeon generator builds underground (the hearth, a hearth ring, a brazier, a wall sconce, an altar fire) gets a vent: a flue carved from just above it up to the surface, straight up where it can, kinked where something is in the way. Carried torches are exempt (the air covers them). A hearth's, a hearth ring's or an altar fire's vent is a shaft, and through it a column of sky-light falls near the fire (design §EV.2: a brazier's or sconce's narrow flue lets in no light worth drawing), cool blue by day and a dim moonlit blue by night, fainter and narrower the deeper the fire; soot stains the stone round the flue's mouth; the fire's flame leans and flickers in the draft. Restart after editing.
_help.surface_y_m: Where the open air is, metres above the hearth room's floor: every flue runs up to it.
_help.max_carve_m: The deepest a fire may be under the surface and still see the sky: a deeper fire's shaft is carved but kinks and twists too much for daylight (a smoke-black hole, no column of light).
_help.light: The shaft of sky-light: day_color / night_color (cool blue, dim moonlit blue), day_energy / night_energy the light falling at the shallowest; attenuation [[depth m, share]...] how much is left at each depth (straight lines between, nothing past the last); beam_alpha the seen shaft of lit air at its brightest (never brighter than its colour, R8), pool_scale how wide the pool of light on the floor is against the flue; sky_glow how bright the sky disc at the flue's top reads looking up. The clock is the world's (a 144-minute day).
_help.soot: Smoke staining painted into the stone round the vent's mouth (its vertex colours: every stone, the ceiling's slabs and the vent's own walls there), navy-black, the colour of smoke.json outlets.soot (§CV.3, §EV.1); it stays when the fire is out: amount 0-1 how black at the middle, size_m across the ceiling round the mouth (a narrow flue's patch smaller), wall_m how far up a sconce's wall the streak reaches.
_help.draft: The air the flue draws: lean_deg how far the flame leans toward the flue at most, flicker how much harder the light flickers, hz how fast the draft breathes.
_help.kink: When something stands over a fire (another piece of the tomb), the flue rises clear_m, then steps sideways up to step_m to find clear rock, and goes on up.
_help.mouth_offset_m: [min, max]: how far a shaft's mouth (over a hearth, a hearth ring, an altar) sits to one side of the fire, in a direction from the seed, so its column of sky-light falls beside the fire, not into it: blue and the fire's warm in one shot. A flue rises straight over its fire; over a sconce, just off its wall.
_help.shaft: §EV.1: the vent of a big fire (for: these fire kinds), a shaft width_m [deepest, shallowest] wide, narrowing with the fire's depth below the surface. Only shafts let daylight down (§EV.2).
_help.flue: §EV.1: the vent of a small fire (for: these kinds), a narrow flue width_m [deepest, shallowest]: it draws the smoke and stains the stone, and lets in no light worth drawing (§EV.2), so a corridor of sconces stays dark between its lights (§BA, §CJ.5).
